name: WebCodecs
role: Frame-exact browser video/audio encoders and decoders; pair with a muxer
summary: Low-level API (VideoEncoder, VideoDecoder, AudioEncoder, ImageDecoder, VideoFrame) for encoding and decoding media without a container. Feed it VideoFrames made from a canvas with explicit timestamps and it returns encoded chunks; a muxer such as Mediabunny writes the file. Frame-exact, unlike MediaRecorder. Needs fully specified codec strings; H.264 availability varies by build.
use_when: Encoding canvas frames to VP9, AV1 or H.264 in-browser with exact timestamps
Decoding source video frames to seek without ffmpeg
Over MediaRecorder when output must not depend on wall-clock time
avoid_when: Finished MP4 with audio mux and filters: ffmpeg
Container reading and writing: Mediabunny or WebAV on top
Cross-engine needs: Firefox support only from v130, so check
notes: 2026-10-26: Codec support in headless Chromium (H.264, AAC) not verified; check isConfigSupported at runtime. MDN page states dedicated-worker availability but not secure-context status.

assessment.rationale: Standard-track, not experimental; Chrome 94 shipped VideoEncoder, VideoDecoder, AudioEncoder and ImageDecoder per MDN browser-compat-data.

evidence.result: VP8 encoder/decoder supported. Two passes each round-tripped 3 32x32 frames at (timestamp,duration) (0,33333),(33333,33333),(66666,33333) us; decoded mean RGB exactly red/green/blue (max channel error 0, tolerance 20). Functional metrics matched on repeat.
evidence.scope: Native WebCodecs VP8 encode/decode of three 32x32 solid frames in Chrome 156; exact timestamps/durations, dimensions and color checked. No muxing or other codecs.
